title: God-conscious Being Centers His Hopes
subtitle: Raag Gauree · Ang 273
summary: This shabad opens with the God-conscious being centers his hopes on the One alone. It turns the heart toward o Nanak, through the God-conscious being, the whole world meditates on God.
whyItMatters: It matters when life feels clingy, possessive, and afraid-to-lose because the shabad keeps attachment inside remembrance, conduct, and the Creator's larger care instead of private momentum.
takeaway: Keep returning to this turn: O Nanak, through the God-conscious being, the whole world meditates on God.

lines.translation: The God-conscious being centers his hopes on the One alone.
The God-conscious being shall never perish.
The God-conscious being is steeped in humility.
The God-conscious being delights in doing good to others.
The God-conscious being has no worldly entanglements.
The God-conscious being holds his wandering mind under control.

lines.gurmukhi: ਬ੍ਰਹਮ ਗਿਆਨੀ ਕੈ ਹੋਇ ਸੁ ਭਲਾ ॥
lines.transliteration: braham giaanee kai hoi su bhalaa ||
lines.translation: The God-conscious being acts in the common good.
The God-conscious being blossoms in fruitfulness.
In the Company of the God-conscious being, all are saved.

lines.gurmukhi: ਨਾਨਕ ਬ੍ਰਹਮ ਗਿਆਨੀ ਜਪੈ ਸਗਲ ਸੰਸਾਰੁ ॥੪॥
lines.transliteration: naanak braham giaanee japai sagal sa(n)saar ||4||
lines.translation: O Nanak, through the God-conscious being, the whole world meditates on God. ||4||

structure: It opens by naming the condition without ornament: the God-conscious being centers his hopes on the One alone.
The middle movement widens the correction through the God-conscious being holds his wandering mind under control.
It closes with a return you can actually keep: o Nanak, through the God-conscious being, the whole world meditates on God.
